trivia_fact: Google published the Bigtable paper in 2006, directly inspiring Apache HBase and influencing the entire NoSQL movement. Bigtable was used internally by Google for Search, Maps, Gmail, and YouTube before becoming a GCP service in 2015.

Anthos was announced at Google Cloud Next 2019 as Google's answer to hybrid and multi-cloud management. Built on Kubernetes and Istio, it can manage workloads across GCP, AWS, Azure, and on-premises — one of the most ambitious multi-cloud plays.

Google's MapReduce paper (2004) launched the big data revolution. It inspired Apache Hadoop, which dominated data processing for a decade. Ironically, Google itself moved on from MapReduce to newer systems like Flume and Dataflow years before Hadoop peaked.

Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) was coined by Ben Treynor Sloss at Google in 2003. He described it as "what happens when you ask a software engineer to design an operations team." The 2016 SRE book became the bible for modern operations practices.
